text:
Rafael Mendes: Staging game day starting now. Goal: simulate partial regional impairment and watch trigger engine + orchestrator behavior end-to-end.

Scope: staging only (us-east-1-stg primary -> us-west-2-stg target).
Roles: IC = me, observers = @Aisha Bello (alerts/SLO), @Mina Haddad (routing), @Ethan Park (control plane), @Victor Alvarez (edge/DNS).
Stop conditions: any unexpected cross-env traffic, auth errors, or sustained 5xx > 5% for > 2m.
Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.inference/display/ONCALL/Automated+Region+Failover+Runbook (staging section)

We’re in monitor-only mode initially. Don’t flip any prod flags please.

incident-bot: Incident channel context set: env=staging, drill=controlled-failover, primary=use1-stg, target=usw2-stg. :information_source:

Miles Thornton: :thumbsup: I’ve got orchestrator UI + audit log open. Trigger engine config is the “gameday-stg” profile.

Aisha Bello: Confirmed. Dashboards open:
- Region health overview (stg): https://grafana.redwood.inference/d/rdw-region-health-stg
- Failover state transitions: https://grafana.redwood.inference/d/rdw-failover-state-stg
Also have burn-rate alert panel muted for the window.

Mina Haddad: Routing policy in stg is pinned to `policy-set: failover-gameday-v3`.
Progressive failover knob is enabled but max 10% in staging (guardrail).

Ethan Park: Control plane is healthy. Orchestrator API ready.
FYI: we rolled a small patch earlier to log safe-to-failover decision inputs (capacity + dependency health) into the audit record.

Rafael Mendes: Step 1: baseline check. Can someone paste current status?

Miles Thornton: Running:
`failoverctl status --env=staging --region=use1-stg`
Output:
```
state: HEALTHY
mode: MONITOR_ONLY
current_action: none
signals:
  p95_latency_ms: 182
  p99_latency_ms: 311
  http_5xx_rate: 0.12%
  queue_depth: 14
  gpu_headroom_pct: 27
  net_probe_loss_pct: 0.0
```
All green.

Sergio Costa: Confirmed no paging. Only “FYI” alert in #eng-sre when we cross warn threshold, but muted.

Rafael Mendes: Step 2: inject impairment. We’re doing “latency + 5xx spike” on the inference gateway in use1-stg.
@Vikram Singh can you apply the chaos rule? (the one that adds 800ms + 2% 5xx to `/v1/chat.completions` only)

Vikram Singh: Yep. Applying now.
Command:
`kubectl -n inference-stg apply -f chaos/impair-use1-chat-800ms-2pct5xx.yaml`

deploy-bot: Applied manifest `chaos/impair-use1-chat-800ms-2pct5xx.yaml` (namespace=inference-stg). Rolling out…

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: chaos injector `impair-use1-chat` is active.

Felix Schneider: Watching state machine panel. Still HEALTHY. Signals starting to move.

Aisha Bello: Seeing p95 creeping: 190 -> 340 -> 610ms. 5xx up to ~0.9% on chat route only.
Tail latency chart looks clean on other routes.

Miles Thornton: Trigger engine evaluation says “DEGRADED candidate” but hasn’t crossed window yet.

Rafael Mendes: Good. Expected: trigger requires 2m window + hysteresis.
Let’s wait for it to cross the degrade threshold.

Mina Haddad: FYI routing policy evaluator is logging “degraded region” annotations but not changing traffic (monitor-only). Good.

Aisha Bello: Now p95=1040ms, p99=2200ms on chat. 5xx ~2.4% chat. Overall 5xx still ~0.6%.
Net probes still fine.

incident-bot: Automated note: Region health score use1-stg dropped below WARN threshold (0.72). No action taken (monitor-only).

Miles Thornton: Trigger engine now shows:
- condition: `chat_tail_latency_high` => true (window=120s)
- condition: `chat_5xx_high` => true (window=120s)
Overall health = DEGRADED.
Orchestrator state remains HEALTHY because monitor-only.

Rafael Mendes: Step 3: flip orchestrator from monitor-only -> active, but only for canary scope.
Change is: enable feature flag `failover.orchestrator.active=true` AND cap to 5% canary for “chat” route in staging.
@Connor O'Brien can you confirm change window ok + who’s flipping?

Connor O'Brien: Window is approved for staging. Please use the release checklist. I can flip flag in LaunchDarkly if someone confirms RBAC is set.
Also reminder: after test, return flag to monitor-only and remove chaos injector.

Ethan Park: RBAC ok for Connor + Rafael in stg. Manual override endpoint should reject anyone else (INT-881 change is in flight for prod, but staging already has it).

Rafael Mendes: Connor please flip. Scope “chat” only, 5% max. We’ll abort if we see any unexpected customer-tier routing.

Connor O'Brien: Done.
LD change: `failover.orchestrator.active` OFF -> ON (env=staging)
Rule: route=chat, max_failover_pct=5, allow_tier=[sandbox, internal]
Audit link: https://console.redwood.inference/stg/audit/changes/ld-flag-78421

incident-bot: Feature flag update detected: `failover.orchestrator.active=true` (env=staging, scope=chat, max=5%).

Felix Schneider: Orchestrator state moved:
HEALTHY -> DEGRADED (enter)
Action queued: progressive_failover_canary(5%)

Miles Thornton: Safe-to-failover checks running…
- target gpu_headroom_pct(usw2-stg)=23% (>= 15% threshold) PASS
- dependency health (policy store, auth, model registry) PASS
- net probes target PASS
Proceeding.

Mina Haddad: Seeing routing policy update proposal in the policy store:
`use1-stg chat` weight 95, `usw2-stg chat` weight 5.
Not applied yet.

Ethan Park: Orchestrator just wrote state transition + decision inputs into audit table.

Victor Alvarez: Edge/DNS not involved for canary (internal routing only). So no TTL propagation issues here.

Sergio Costa: Metrics confirm 4.8-5.1% chat traffic now landing in usw2-stg. Latency for canary cohort is back to baseline.

Aisha Bello: This is good: overall error rate drops slightly as we bleed off chat traffic.
But I’m seeing one weird thing: dashboard “customer impact by tier” shows enterprise tier getting 0.3% of reroute (?) even though scope should be sandbox/internal.
Can someone verify label mapping?

Mina Haddad: I think that’s a dashboard query bug. In staging, `tier` label is blank for internal synthetic traffic and the panel defaults blanks into “enterprise” bucket (ugh).
@Sergio Costa can you sanity check PromQL?

Sergio Costa: Yep found it. Panel uses `label_replace` that maps empty to “enterprise” (copied from prod assumptions). I’ll fix the stg dashboard and open a PR in observability-pack.
Immediate workaround: filter `source="synthetic"`.

Felix Schneider: State machine stable. No flapping. Hold-down timer not triggered.

Rafael Mendes: Great catch. Call it out as follow-up.
Next step: increase impairment to trigger FAILOVER threshold (not just degraded) and see if it escalates to 25% (still in staging guardrail).
Miles, what’s the configured max for this drill?

Miles Thornton: For staging drill profile:
- DEGRADED => 5% canary
- FAILED => ramp to 25% (max)
No full failover allowed in stg without a manual override.

Rafael Mendes: Perfect. @Vikram Singh please bump chaos to 8% 5xx on chat and add packet loss 3% at ingress (use1-stg only).

Vikram Singh: Applying updated chaos rules.
`kubectl -n inference-stg apply -f chaos/impair-use1-chat-800ms-8pct5xx.yaml`
`kubectl -n edge-stg apply -f chaos/impair-use1-ingress-3pct-loss.yaml`

deploy-bot: Applied manifest `chaos/impair-use1-chat-800ms-8pct5xx.yaml`.

deploy-bot: Applied manifest `chaos/impair-use1-ingress-3pct-loss.yaml`.

Aisha Bello: Now we’re definitely failing. Chat 5xx is ~7-9%. Streaming disconnects up. p99 is ugly.

incident-bot: Automated note: Region health score use1-stg dropped below FAIL threshold (0.39). Orchestrator evaluating escalation.

Miles Thornton: Trigger engine: FAILED (window satisfied).
Orchestrator proposes: progressive_failover_ramp(to=25%).
Safe-to-failover check is FAILING right now: target queue_depth(usw2-stg) spiked.
Queue_depth=980 (> 800 threshold).
It’s saying “NOT SAFE TO FAILOVER: target saturation risk”.

Harish Reddy: Looking. That queue spike is from the load test job we left running in usw2-stg (my bad). I’m stopping it now.

Harish Reddy: Stopped job `llm-batch-loadgen` in usw2-stg. Queue should drain in ~1-2 min.

Mina Haddad: Nice, that’s exactly why we wanted the safety check.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. Note for retro: “safe-to-failover prevented bad move due to background loadgen”.
Let’s wait until queue_depth < 200 and see if it proceeds.

Felix Schneider: Orchestrator stays in FAILED but action is “blocked_by_safety_check”. No state flapping.

Miles Thornton: Queue_depth now 460… 310… 190.
Safety check flips to PASS.
Orchestrator applying ramp to 25%.

Ethan Park: Control plane logs show:
`applyRoutingWeights(route=chat, from=use1-stg, to=usw2-stg, weight=25) ok`

Sergio Costa: Traffic split confirmed at 24-26% to usw2-stg.
Latency for the diverted cohort is fine.
But we’re seeing elevated auth errors only in usw2-stg for ~0.2% requests (`401 invalid audience`). That’s new.

Ethan Park: That’s probably a staging-only misconfig in the token validator: audience list missing `chat-stg` for usw2.
We should not continue escalating with auth errors.

Rafael Mendes: Stop condition hit. Roll back to 5% and then remove impairment.
Connor can you set max back to 5% and/or return to degraded action only?

Connor O'Brien: Dropping cap to 5% now via flag rule update.
LD change: max_failover_pct 25 -> 5.

incident-bot: Feature flag update detected: `max_failover_pct=5%` (env=staging, scope=chat).

Mina Haddad: Routing weights updated back to 95/5.

Vikram Singh: Removing chaos injectors.
`kubectl -n inference-stg delete -f chaos/impair-use1-chat-800ms-8pct5xx.yaml`
`kubectl -n edge-stg delete -f chaos/impair-use1-ingress-3pct-loss.yaml`

deploy-bot: Deleted manifest `chaos/impair-use1-chat-800ms-8pct5xx.yaml`.

deploy-bot: Deleted manifest `chaos/impair-use1-ingress-3pct-loss.yaml`.

Aisha Bello: Signals recovering. Chat p95 back to ~210ms, 5xx back <0.2%. Net probes normal.

Felix Schneider: Orchestrator state transitioned FAILED -> DEGRADED -> HEALTHY (with exit hysteresis, nice).
Audit log shows blocked escalation due to queue_depth; then proceeded; then manual cap reduction.

Rafael Mendes: Great. Ending drill.
Action items / follow-ups:
1) Fix dashboard tier mapping bug (staging blanks shown as enterprise). @Sergio Costa to PR.
2) Investigate auth audience misconfig in usw2-stg token validator for chat route. @Ethan Park please file/assign.
3) Add explicit pre-flight check in game day checklist: “no background loadgen in target region”. @Harish Reddy we’ll update checklist.
4) Confirm safe-to-failover queue_depth threshold is correct (800). Might want dynamic threshold based on instance count.

Please drop any other observations here.

Sergio Costa: +1. I’ll open PR + link it. Also suggest adding an annotation event when safety check blocks (right now it’s only in audit logs).

Miles Thornton: Noted: trigger engine logs are hard to correlate across components. We should add `decision_id` to routing policy write + dashboard.

Mina Haddad: Also: policy store write took ~6s on ramp. Not terrible, but we should track it.

Ethan Park: I’ll file the auth audience issue. Also we should add a “dependency gating” check for auth config parity between regions (at least in stg).

Victor Alvarez: No DNS involved today, but when we do DNS-based drill we need to bake in TTL + caching expectations. Different game day.

incident-bot: Incident marked as resolved (drill). Summary captured in audit trail. Next step: link follow-up tickets in post-drill retro doc.
